messages:
maria: Quick sync — need to align on boundary ownership + tenant evacuation scenarios for the multi-region rollout. Who owns the playbook and what's an acceptable RTO?

jon: High level: infra owns routing primitives, eng-platform owns rollout automation, SRE owns runbook/ops playbook, product owns customer contract. We should document.

rachel: Agree with ownership split. Can we enumerate scenarios? e.g., region failure, tenant QoS spike, noisy neighbor, data residency/legal evacuation.

sam: List: 1) full region evac (az/region down), 2) soft spill (latency spike), 3) tenant-level quarantine (abuse/compliance), 4) jurisdictional migrate (data residency constraint).

leo: For each we need: trigger conditions, routing policy, rollback criteria, observable signals, and acceptance test.

maria: Proposal: classify evac types as FAST (automated, <60s), WARM (guided, <5m), MANUAL (>5m). Assign default owners and SLOs per class. Thoughts?

jon: +1. FAST should be infra only (auto-failover to replica region + KV cache invalidation pattern). WARM needs platform + SRE to coordinate stateful tenants. MANUAL is product+security for policy moves.

rachel: Important: define what "evacuated" means for stateful workloads. Is it traffic-only reroute or data movement? We need both spelled out in playbook.

sam: Agreed. For stateful: traffic reroute first, then async data replication or restricted read-only mode depending on contract.

leo: Draft playbook snippet (for FAST):
```
trigger: control-plane-heartbeat-miss > 3
action: route->region-b with prefix-kw-cache-flush
rollback: control-plane-heartbeat-restored && 5m stable
observability: 95th latency, error-rate, replica-queue-depth
```

maria: Nice. Also add cost guard: don't evacuate to dedicated-priority pool without approval if predicted cost > 2x.

jon: We need launch gating criteria:
- RFC + owner assigned
- Simulated evac test in staging (inject 5% traffic fail -> measure RTO)
- Perf regressions <5% p95 during fallback
- SRE runbook + runbook playthrough by oncall

rachel: And customer-facing acceptance: documented behavior, SLA notes in contract language, and a per-tenant opt-out flag for forced evacuation if they need stricter isolation.

sam: Ops checklist: runbook link, canary plan, telemetry dashboard (evac events), postmortem template.

infra-bot: canary-deploy: started canary of routing-policy-v2 to canary-slice-03 (logs: https://logs/routing/1755552468).

leo: Action items: 1) maria to own RFC + initial playbook draft (due EOD Thu). 2) jon to define infra primitives required (k8s svc, lb weight, cache flush API). 3) rachel + sam to draft acceptance tests. 4) SRE to schedule playthrough.

maria: I'll create RFC today and ping owners. If no major objections we'll fold into Q3 architecture sprint. :thumbsup:

jon: One more: add a matrix for tenant categories (PLG/free, paying, enterprise with contractual isolation) and permitted evac strategies per category.

rachel: Good call. That matrix will drive both cost and SLA decisions.

sam: No objections. Will start test harness for simulated failovers tomorrow.

maria: Thanks all — filing RFC now. Will @mention when draft ready for review.

leo: FYI we should also include a minimal code sample for the SDK to surface "evacuation-mode" to customers so they can degrade gracefully.

maria: noted. End of thread.
